correctness.rationale: Uniform sampling on the permutational wreath product makes the top action and base coordinates independent and uniform. Identity top action takes the maximum of p base order exponents. A nonidentity top action is a single p-cycle (primality is used); its p-th power has conjugate coordinate cycle products, each uniform, so the order exponent is one plus that of a uniform base-group element. This proves the stated CDF and tail recurrences with the boundary T_{h,r}=1 for h≤r and T_{h,0}=α^h. After normalization by α^h, the increment is α^(-1)S_{h-1,r-1} plus O_p(α^{h-2} S_{h-1,r-1}²); for each fixed r the induction bounds this error by a summable exponential times a polynomial. Summing the preceding degree-(r−1) main term gives the coefficient 1/(r!α^r) and an O_{p,r}(h^{r−1}) remainder. Subtracting the next smaller tail preserves the relative O_{p,r}(1/h) estimate, and at r=0 no subtraction is needed. For p=2 and r=1, each normalized increment at h≥2 is 2−2^{1-h}; summation from S_{1,1}=2 gives the stated exact binary formula. The group size follows from |W_h|=p|W_{h-1}|^p, and the construction attains exponent p^h.
residual_risks: Only fixed p and r are covered. Finite permutation-order counts and floating-point ratios are not asymptotic proof; the supplied checker was not executed.

The independently supported contribution is the exact leading coefficient and relative error at every fixed defect in the exponentially small uniform-element tail. The nearest same-group primary theorems treated typical-order scale or a different sampling measure; the published neighbouring records do not cover the all-depth rare-tail regime.

value.rationale: Element orders are intrinsic statistics of this Sylow tower. A distribution concentrated on a typical linear scale leaves open how many elements attain or nearly attain exponent at depth h. The result separates each fixed defect by an additional polynomial factor and computes the factorial constant on the rare exponential scale, addressing a natural boundary regime across all primes. It is more than recovering counts at a few finite depths or reading off a branching speed.
residual_risks: No claim of a typical-order improvement, growing-defect law or further structural application is needed or made.
